evidence.claim: In August 2020, two teenagers found gasoline bubbling from the ground in Oehler Nature Preserve near Huntersville.
evidence.quote: On August 14, 2020, two teenagers were riding all-terrain vehicles in the Oehler Nature Preserve in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, when they noticed a puddle of gasoline bubbling up from the ground.

evidence.claim: The leak came from the buried Colonial Pipeline.
evidence.quote: The gasoline was coming from a leak in the Colonial Pipeline

evidence.claim: Colonial later reported that its pipeline had failed on July 27, at least eighteen days before the discovery.
evidence.quote: According to the company, the pipeline had failed on July 27, 2020, meaning that gasoline had been leaking from the spot for at least 18 days prior to its discovery.

evidence.claim: In July 2022, the company estimated that at least two million gallons had escaped.
evidence.quote: on July 22, as per the terms of the consent decree, the company put out a statement saying that they now estimated that at least 2,000,000 U.S. gal (7,600,000 L) had leaked

evidence.claim: That month, a court approved a consent decree requiring further testing, a cleanup plan and penalties.
evidence.quote: The settlement was approved by Judge Kimberly Best on July 7.
